evidence.excerpt: WFP said nearly one third of Bangladesh's population faced food insecurity and 20 percent lived below the national poverty line; since 2017 it had been providing food assistance and nutrition services in the Cox's Bazar Rohingya camps and surrounding community, along with life-skills training, disaster-risk-reduction activities, and engineering services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary WFP overview page summarizing the country's vulnerability and program response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level context under the Hasina administration; the source does not attribute the conditions to one person specifically.
contrary_evidence: The page emphasizes significant economic growth, so the food-insecurity figures do not imply total policy failure but they do show major unmet need.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said more than 1.5 million children were at increased risk from flooding in north-eastern Bangladesh and that it was on the ground with government and non-government partners to meet urgent safety, health, nutrition, clean-water, and education needs; UNICEF was also supporting the government flood response with water purification tablets, hygiene kits, therapeutic milk, learning kits, and social workers.
evidence.title: Over 1.5 million children at risk as devastating floods hit Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said more than 1.5 million children were at increased risk from flooding in north-eastern Bangladesh and that it was on the ground with government and non-government partners to meet urgent safety, health, nutrition, clean-water, and education needs; UNICEF was also supporting the government flood response with water purification tablets, hygiene kits, therapeutic milk, learning kits, and social workers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF emergency response statement with concrete numbers and response actions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect government response context under the Hasina administration, not a personal act by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The same report shows the scale of harm: over four million people were affected, schools were submerged, and children were losing learning time.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said extreme poverty in Bangladesh fell to 5 percent in 2022 from 9 percent in 2016, and that other wellbeing measures also improved, including infant mortality, stunting, access to electricity, sanitary toilets, and education; rural areas saw faster poverty reduction than urban areas, though urban inequality widened.
evidence.title: Structural Reforms are Essential to Sustain Growth & Poverty Reduction in Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said extreme poverty in Bangladesh fell to 5 percent in 2022 from 9 percent in 2016, and that other wellbeing measures also improved, including infant mortality, stunting, access to electricity, sanitary toilets, and education; rural areas saw faster poverty reduction than urban areas, though urban inequality widened.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank retrospective on 2022 poverty and wellbeing outcomes with explicit metrics.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Outcome-level evidence under the Hasina administration, not direct proof of a specific personal decision.
contrary_evidence: The same article says sustaining growth requires policy adjustments and notes balance-of-payments pressure, rising inflation, and financial-sector vulnerabilities.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said Bangladesh's flagship Mother and Child Benefit Programme covered 1.25 million beneficiaries in 2022-23 and was planned to expand to 4 million by 2023-24 and 6 million by 2026; it also said the child budget share remained stagnant at 15.05 percent and identified low utilization and rushed end-of-year spending as implementation challenges.
evidence.title: Public Finance for Children
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said Bangladesh's flagship Mother and Child Benefit Programme covered 1.25 million beneficiaries in 2022-23 and was planned to expand to 4 million by 2023-24 and 6 million by 2026; it also said the child budget share remained stagnant at 15.05 percent and identified low utilization and rushed end-of-year spending as implementation challenges.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF policy note with explicit program coverage, financing, and implementation critique.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect government policy under the Hasina administration; the note is not a personal directive by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The same note says child-budget shares were stagnant and implementation suffered from low utilization and rushed spending, so it is mixed rather than a clean success story.

evidence.claim: The WHO/UNICEF report said 51 percent of surveyed parents and pregnant women had been targeted by formula-milk marketing; in Bangladesh, 65 percent of women exclusively breastfed up to five months and 98 percent wanted to breastfeed, yet the report called for stronger enforcement of Bangladesh's national code legislation and breastfeeding support.
evidence.title: Progress on breastfeeding in Bangladesh undermined by aggressive formula milk marketing - WHO, UNICEF
evidence.excerpt: The WHO/UNICEF report said 51 percent of surveyed parents and pregnant women had been targeted by formula-milk marketing; in Bangladesh, 65 percent of women exclusively breastfed up to five months and 98 percent wanted to breastfeed, yet the report called for stronger enforcement of Bangladesh's national code legislation and breastfeeding support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary WHO/UNICEF report with Bangladesh-specific data and a clear policy recommendation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly system-level rather than personal attribution; useful as evidence of regulatory gap under the Hasina administration.
contrary_evidence: The source shows strong breastfeeding intent among families, so the problem is partly regulatory and enforcement-related rather than simply behavioral.

evidence.claim: The Survey on Street Children 2022 found that children living on the street in Bangladesh faced deprivation, extreme poverty, malnutrition, disease, illiteracy, and violence; UNICEF said the numbers could be in the millions and that it was working with the government as it invested in more social workers to help children leave the streets.
evidence.title: UNICEF: New report details shocking deprivation of children living on the street
evidence.excerpt: The Survey on Street Children 2022 found that children living on the street in Bangladesh faced deprivation, extreme poverty, malnutrition, disease, illiteracy, and violence; UNICEF said the numbers could be in the millions and that it was working with the government as it invested in more social workers to help children leave the streets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF release based on a 2022 survey with specific vulnerability and harm indicators.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect government context under the Hasina administration; the source does not isolate one decision-maker but does identify the need for state response.
contrary_evidence: The report is about severe unmet need, so it is mainly negative evidence even though it also notes government social-worker involvement.

evidence.claim: Hasina publicly said Bangladeshi media could say whatever they wished and that criticism remained free, while answering a question about the Digital Security Act.
evidence.title: Media in Bangladesh free to criticise my government: PM Hasina
evidence.excerpt: Hasina publicly said Bangladeshi media could say whatever they wished and that criticism remained free, while answering a question about the Digital Security Act.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a direct public statement by the ruler with clear date and context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct public statement by Sheikh Hasina about her own government's media environment.
contrary_evidence: HRW and Freedom House documented journalist arrests, self-censorship, and DSA-based pressure in the same period.

evidence.claim: Hasina said free and fair elections had only happened under Awami League rule and told the BBC to judge disappearance allegations by how true they were.
evidence.title: Free, fair polls held only during AL govt, PM Hasina tells BBC
evidence.excerpt: Hasina said free and fair elections had only happened under Awami League rule and told the BBC to judge disappearance allegations by how true they were.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report of an interview statement by the ruler, with exact quoted claims and a dated interview context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct public statement by Sheikh Hasina about elections and disappearances during her tenure.
contrary_evidence: Freedom House and HRW described manipulated elections, pressure on critics, and unresolved disappearance allegations.

evidence.claim: Hasina urged supporters to counter what she called propaganda and described critics as spreading false and fabricated information about Bangladesh and her government.
evidence.title: PM asks to give befitting reply to anti-Bangladesh propaganda
evidence.excerpt: Hasina urged supporters to counter what she called propaganda and described critics as spreading false and fabricated information about Bangladesh and her government.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official wire report of a direct ruler statement with clear date, but the claim is self-serving and needs corroboration by contrary evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct public statement by Sheikh Hasina; the claim concerns her own government and its critics.
contrary_evidence: Independent reporting in 2022 documented the government's retaliation against critics, activists, and rights groups.

evidence.claim: Hasina said the Awami League never violates human rights and instead protects rights.
evidence.title: AL government never violates human rights
evidence.excerpt: Hasina said the Awami League never violates human rights and instead protects rights.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous quotation reported in a wire summary; exact wording is recoverable from the snippet, though not from an open page fetch.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct public statement by Sheikh Hasina about her own party's conduct.
contrary_evidence: HRW, Freedom House, and UN-related reporting in 2022 documented arbitrary arrests, repression, and impunity.

evidence.claim: The government cancelled Odhikar's registration after the group documented disappearances and killings, and the letter said the organization spread misleading information that tarnished the state's image.
evidence.title: Govt scraps Odhikar’s registration
evidence.excerpt: The government cancelled Odhikar's registration after the group documented disappearances and killings, and the letter said the organization spread misleading information that tarnished the state's image.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed contemporaneous reporting with a copy of the official letter and specific administrative action against a rights group.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The action was taken by a bureau under the government led by Hasina; it directly targeted a group documenting state abuses.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes Odhikar was one of the few groups systematically logging disappearances, so the government's rationale is contested.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that Hasina rewarded sanctioned RAB and police officials with promotions and medals instead of accountability, and the government sent one sanctioned police chief to a UN event to bypass a US travel ban.
evidence.title: Bangladesh Government Keeps Rewarding Rights Abusers
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that Hasina rewarded sanctioned RAB and police officials with promotions and medals instead of accountability, and the government sent one sanctioned police chief to a UN event to bypass a US travel ban.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed contemporaneous NGO reporting that ties the action to named sanctioned officials and to Hasina's own awards and government decisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Hasina and her government through awards, promotions, and delegation decisions involving sanctioned loyalists.
contrary_evidence: The government claimed business as usual and reform was unnecessary, which reinforces rather than weakens the abuse pattern.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh decided to send police chief Benazir Ahmed to a UN summit even though the US had sanctioned him for human-rights violations.
evidence.title: Govt to send IGP Benazir to UN event
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh decided to send police chief Benazir Ahmed to a UN summit even though the US had sanctioned him for human-rights violations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific, dated report of an official government decision involving a sanctioned official and public funds.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government action under Hasina's cabinet; it shows tolerance and validation of a sanctioned loyalist.
contrary_evidence: The article itself notes the US sanctions and the government's effort to work around them, which cuts against any claim of accountability.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said unqualified Awami League loyalists were alleged to be getting court positions, and that cases against ruling-party activists were regularly withdrawn for 'political consideration'.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said unqualified Awami League loyalists were alleged to be getting court positions, and that cases against ruling-party activists were regularly withdrawn for 'political consideration'.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Established country report with explicit claims about judicial politicization and preferential treatment for ruling-party actors.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: it describes patronage and impunity patterns under the AL government led by Hasina, not a single personal act.
contrary_evidence: These are allegations and structural observations rather than a direct finding of Hasina's personal intent in one discrete case.

evidence.claim: HRW said the government used the Digital Security Act to harass and detain critics, targeted family members of diaspora journalists, denied disappearance findings, and reacted to spyware allegations by offering a peacekeeping explanation the UN rejected.
evidence.title: World Report 2022: Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: HRW said the government used the Digital Security Act to harass and detain critics, targeted family members of diaspora journalists, denied disappearance findings, and reacted to spyware allegations by offering a peacekeeping explanation the UN rejected.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual country report with multiple specific mechanisms of concealment, retaliation, and official denial tied to Hasina's government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The abuses are attributed to the Awami League-led government under Hasina; the report also records official denial and an implausible cover explanation from security officials.
contrary_evidence: The government's denials and the UN's rejection of the equipment explanation are themselves evidence against candor.

evidence.claim: The government appointed career finance secretary Abdur Rouf Talukder, who had decades of public-finance experience, as Bangladesh Bank governor.
evidence.title: Bangladesh appoints Abdur Rouf Talukder as central bank governor
evidence.excerpt: The government appointed career finance secretary Abdur Rouf Talukder, who had decades of public-finance experience, as Bangladesh Bank governor.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Clear, dated appointment notice with a professional biography and no apparent controversy in the appointment itself.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Hasina's government made the appointment; this is a modest positive counterexample to a pure-cronyism narrative.
contrary_evidence: A single professional appointment does not show broader independence or honesty across the government.

evidence.claim: The Anti-Corruption Commission opened a probe alleging that Hasina, during her tenure as prime minister, misused authority to allocate six government plots to herself and close family members.
evidence.title: ACC probes land allocation allegations involving Sheikh Hasina, family
evidence.excerpt: The Anti-Corruption Commission opened a probe alleging that Hasina, during her tenure as prime minister, misused authority to allocate six government plots to herself and close family members.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Later but specific investigative reporting tied to an official probe, with direct allegations about family benefit and misuse of authority.
evidence.period_fit: retrospective about conduct during Hasina's tenure; not a discrete 2022 event
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong family/office nexus: the allegations describe personal benefit to Hasina and relatives through government land allocation while she was in office.
contrary_evidence: This is an allegation/probe, not a final judicial finding, so it should be treated cautiously.

evidence.claim: The Eighth Five Year Plan blends COVID-19 recovery strategies into the macroeconomic framework and aims to implement Perspective Plan 2021-2041 so Bangladesh can reach upper-middle-income status by 2031 and eliminate extreme poverty by 2031.
evidence.title: 8th Five Year Plan (English Version)
evidence.publisher: General Economics Division, Bangladesh Planning Commission
evidence.excerpt: The Eighth Five Year Plan blends COVID-19 recovery strategies into the macroeconomic framework and aims to implement Perspective Plan 2021-2041 so Bangladesh can reach upper-middle-income status by 2031 and eliminate extreme poverty by 2031.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct government planning document from the responsible planning body with explicit objectives and timeline.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 planning document for the target period
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: this is the government planning apparatus under Hasina's administration.
contrary_evidence: It is a plan statement, not proof of later delivery by itself.

evidence.claim: Hasina announced that her government would build Smart Bangladesh by 2041 and said the strategy rests on smart citizens, smart economy, smart government, and smart society.
evidence.title: From 'Digital Bangladesh' to 'Smart Bangladesh' by 2041: PM
evidence.excerpt: Hasina announced that her government would build Smart Bangladesh by 2041 and said the strategy rests on smart citizens, smart economy, smart government, and smart society.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a direct public announcement by the ruler with clear date and context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: Hasina announced the goal herself as head of government.
contrary_evidence: Announcement is not the same as economy-wide implementation.

evidence.claim: The Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 frames a 100-year vision for a safe, climate-resilient and prosperous delta and a mission to ensure long-term water and food security, economic growth, and environmental sustainability.
evidence.title: Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100: Issues and Challenges of Implementation, 2022 conference page
evidence.excerpt: The Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 frames a 100-year vision for a safe, climate-resilient and prosperous delta and a mission to ensure long-term water and food security, economic growth, and environmental sustainability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official planning portal summarizing the national strategy in plain language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the plan is state strategy under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: The page sets goals and mission, not outcomes.

evidence.claim: A Delta Governing Council chaired by the prime minister had been set up to implement the Delta Plan 2100 through policy making, strategic direction, investment planning, and Delta Fund setup.
evidence.title: Delta Governing Council (DGC)
evidence.excerpt: A Delta Governing Council chaired by the prime minister had been set up to implement the Delta Plan 2100 through policy making, strategic direction, investment planning, and Delta Fund setup.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government implementation page describing the governing body and its duties.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong: this is PM-chaired institutional machinery created under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: Institutional setup does not by itself prove effective execution.

evidence.claim: The Power Division won the Digital Bangladesh Award 2022 for ERP implementation that improved efficiency, transparency, accountability, and customer service, and the article says the system had been implemented across 15 subordinate bodies.
evidence.title: Power Division receives 'Digital Bangladesh Award 2022'
evidence.excerpt: The Power Division won the Digital Bangladesh Award 2022 for ERP implementation that improved efficiency, transparency, accountability, and customer service, and the article says the system had been implemented across 15 subordinate bodies.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting with concrete implementation details and a named award.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government operational line under Hasina; the article credits agency-level execution more than personal micromanagement.
contrary_evidence: The benefits are reported by the division and the article, not independently audited in this item.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh's 20-month COVID-19 school closures led the Ministry of Education to create a remote learning strategy using television, radio, digital lessons, and printed materials that supported 150,933 children from marginalized groups in 842 schools.
evidence.title: Learning from the education sector’s COVID-19 response to prepare for future emergencies (Bangladesh)
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh's 20-month COVID-19 school closures led the Ministry of Education to create a remote learning strategy using television, radio, digital lessons, and printed materials that supported 150,933 children from marginalized groups in 842 schools.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF summary of a ministry-led response with explicit coverage figures and delivery channels.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Ministry of Education action under the Hasina government; this is not direct personal micromanagement.
contrary_evidence: The measure was a partial response to severe school disruption, not full continuity of schooling.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Bangladesh had achieved impressive growth and social development but still needed productive investment in infrastructure, human capital, and climate resilience to reach upper-middle-income status in 2031.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: 2021 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Bangladesh had achieved impressive growth and social development but still needed productive investment in infrastructure, human capital, and climate resilience to reach upper-middle-income status in 2031.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IMF country report summary with explicit policy and target language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but clear: the report addresses the authorities' stated development path under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes pandemic interruptions, slowing poverty reduction, and financial vulnerabilities.

evidence.claim: The IMF and Bangladesh authorities reached a staff-level agreement for a new program aimed at preserving macroeconomic stability, supporting inclusive and green growth, and protecting the vulnerable, after reserves fell and the current-account deficit widened.
evidence.title: IMF Staff Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with Bangladesh on the Extended Credit Facility/Extended Fund Facility and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility
evidence.excerpt: The IMF and Bangladesh authorities reached a staff-level agreement for a new program aimed at preserving macroeconomic stability, supporting inclusive and green growth, and protecting the vulnerable, after reserves fell and the current-account deficit widened.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IMF press release with concrete program design and contemporaneous macro stress context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the agreement was with the Bangladesh authorities led by Hasina's cabinet and central bank team.
contrary_evidence: The article also records reserve loss, inflation, and import-pressure stress, which constrain claims of clean success.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh navigated the COVID-19 pandemic with prudent macroeconomic policies and real GDP growth rebounded to 7.1 percent in FY22, supported by pandemic containment, domestic and external demand, and government stimulus packages and policy support.
evidence.title: Sustaining Growth in Bangladesh with Strong Reforms
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh navigated the COVID-19 pandemic with prudent macroeconomic policies and real GDP growth rebounded to 7.1 percent in FY22, supported by pandemic containment, domestic and external demand, and government stimulus packages and policy support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank feature with explicit FY22 growth data and policy attribution, though still a retrospective synthesis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the growth rebound is policy-associated but also partly reflects inherited recovery and external demand.
contrary_evidence: The same source stresses inflation, BoP deficits, reserve pressure, and financial-sector vulnerabilities.

evidence.claim: Extreme poverty in Bangladesh fell to 5.0 percent in 2022 from 9.0 percent in 2016, with improved infant mortality, stunting, electricity access, sanitary toilets, and education access, though inequality and macro pressures persisted.
evidence.title: Structural Reforms are Essential to Sustain Growth & Poverty Reduction in Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: Extreme poverty in Bangladesh fell to 5.0 percent in 2022 from 9.0 percent in 2016, with improved infant mortality, stunting, electricity access, sanitary toilets, and education access, though inequality and macro pressures persisted.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank feature based on 2022 household survey data and linked development update, with a methodological note.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate and limited: the gains reflect long-run growth and policy support rather than one 2022 decision alone.
contrary_evidence: The report notes methodological changes in the 2022 survey and still flags inflation, reserve pressure, and financial-sector vulnerabilities.

evidence.claim: According to documents reviewed by the ACC, Sheikh Hasina was granted a 10-katha Purbachal plot on August 3, 2022 in her own name, and her son, daughter, sister, and her sister’s two children each received 10-katha plots as well.
evidence.title: ACC finds proof of 'abuse of power' in plots for Hasina, family
evidence.excerpt: According to documents reviewed by the ACC, Sheikh Hasina was granted a 10-katha Purbachal plot on August 3, 2022 in her own name, and her son, daughter, sister, and her sister’s two children each received 10-katha plots as well.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reports ACC documents rather than only allegation, but remains a news account of an ongoing inquiry rather than a final judgment.
evidence.period_fit: Directly concerns 2022 plot allocations to Hasina and close family.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for personal nexus: the plot was issued in Hasina’s name and the family allocations are tied to her family; the article still stops short of a final adjudication of guilt.
contrary_evidence: The ACC investigation was still ongoing in the article, so the finding is evidentiary rather than final judicial proof.

evidence.claim: RAJUK sources said plot applications were routed to the Prime Minister’s Office and that, with Sheikh Hasina’s consent, the PMO decided who would get the plot; the article also says Hasina and six family members each received 10-katha plots and that the family paid in 2022.
evidence.title: Hasina awarded 830 plots to 'loyalists and sycophants'
evidence.excerpt: RAJUK sources said plot applications were routed to the Prime Minister’s Office and that, with Sheikh Hasina’s consent, the PMO decided who would get the plot; the article also says Hasina and six family members each received 10-katha plots and that the family paid in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contains direct sourcing to RAJUK sources and a concrete allocation narrative, but it is still journalistic reconstruction rather than the underlying administrative file.
evidence.period_fit: The claim explicitly ties the plot allocations and payment to 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong: the article attributes recipient selection to PMO action taken with Hasina’s consent, which is the closest direct nexus recovered in this round.
contrary_evidence: The consent claim is reported through RAJUK sources, not published as the primary internal memo itself.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that a leaked government circular apparently signed by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and the cabinet secretary tasked the Finance Ministry and the Prime Minister’s Office with monitoring foreign funding to several human rights organizations after the US sanctions.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Stop Reprisals Against Victims, Activists
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that a leaked government circular apparently signed by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and the cabinet secretary tasked the Finance Ministry and the Prime Minister’s Office with monitoring foreign funding to several human rights organizations after the US sanctions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The reporting is contemporaneous and specific, but it uses the qualifier 'apparently signed,' so the signature is not independently authenticated in the article itself.
evidence.period_fit: Directly contemporaneous with early 2022 retaliation after the 2021 sanctions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but not absolute: the article ties the circular to Hasina’s apparent signature and to PMO-level action, which supports personal nexus while leaving some verification uncertainty.
contrary_evidence: The source does not independently publish the circular itself or forensic authentication of the signature.

evidence.claim: HRW said Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina offered promotions and rewards to security-force commanders implicated in grave abuses instead of accountability, and that the government made sanctioned police chief Benazir Ahmed part of an official UN delegation to bypass the US travel ban.
evidence.title: Bangladesh Government Keeps Rewarding Rights Abusers
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina offered promotions and rewards to security-force commanders implicated in grave abuses instead of accountability, and that the government made sanctioned police chief Benazir Ahmed part of an official UN delegation to bypass the US travel ban.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific, contemporaneous, and directly tied to Hasina by name, but still a rights-monitoring account rather than an internal directive record.
evidence.period_fit: Entirely within 2022 and tied to the year’s sanctions-response and appointment decisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for personal nexus on the reward side because Hasina is named as the actor offering medals/promotions; the delegation decision is government action but still a close-network choice.
contrary_evidence: The article does not provide a signed order from Hasina for each personnel move, so subordinate implementation remains part of the chain.
